contradictions_preserved: The donor already stores and schema-enforces strong per-retrieval causal identities, yet the Stop model-judge path discards those stronger keys during target selection and falls back to session plus recency.

The donor has an exact retrieval_id lookup for explicit human judgement, showing exact target binding is already a working local pattern, while automatic model relevance uses the weaker newest-session path.

Receipt hashing is deterministic after row selection, but the credit value participates in the hash and retrieval_feedback lacks a visible UNIQUE(retrieval_id, signal_class); therefore two different model judgements for the same retrieval are not proven impossible by schema or receipt identity alone. Runtime reachability remains unmeasured.
counterhypotheses: Host hook serialization may make concurrent same-session Stop selection unreachable in the installed runtime.
SQLite write locking or higher-level host ordering may suppress practical double-credit even though no dedicated per-retrieval model-judgement uniqueness constraint is visible.
A single retrieval per user turn plus strictly ordered Stop delivery may keep transcript-latest and newest retrieval aligned in normal operation.
